g.text: ArthurRank6Convo4 begins.
Odd question. Do they have toys in space?
Like, children's toys? Of course.
What... kind of toys?
Heh. Really?
OH, SOL. That's not what I meant, and you know it!
Hard to picture some umpteenth-some-odd-whatever thousands of years in the future,
I mean, children's toys. Dolls. Action figures. Things like that.
Kids are still sitting around reenacting stories with little figurines and playing "bandits" or "save the princess."
Just giving you a hard time. :P
No, we don't. [End.]
What brought this on?
What did you grow up playing with?
We have different names for the games we play, but I definitely had toys.
Yeah, of course we do.
Chat ends.
I was actually watching Amir playing one of his arcade games.
It's rather comforting thinking that despite all the differences between our cultures, kids still just... sit down and play with toys.
Like what?
And I was thinking to myself - what I wouldn't give to have that kind of joy in my life again.
I had this action figure. Action Angus. He was a soldier, no surprise there.
All sorts of figurines, and stuffed animals, and blocks. Typical kid stuff.
I had this one - I guess you could call it a figurine - of this Dax child, that, well, I named after a character in a book I had. Dominus Thrax.
I've never looked down my nose at Aoi, or Amir, or even now Kaya for finding fun in "childish" things. It's never bothered me.
One solstice celebration, a bunch of the older boys stole it from me along with a bunch of my other toys and, well...
Oh, bollocks. I should've known. I'm so sorry that I brought this up.
But sometimes I'm afraid that the part of me that's capable of feeling that curled up and died a long time ago.
It's a long story. Short of it? I was "too old," they said, to be playing with dollies. That was the last time I ever played with toys.
Not the best topic for me to discuss, no.
It's all right. It's not your fault.
Kind of sad, isn't it? That we tell children to love something, and then we tell them to give it up when they've "matured."

The other day, I was watching Amir play one of his games. It's clear how much he's attached it. How much happiness it brings him. And I was a bit jealous that I don't have anything like that in my life.
Now I feel like an absolute knobhead.
We had all the normal toys you'd expect, I suppose. Blocks, stuffed animals, figurines, dolls.
I don't know. We all have to grow up sometime. We can't hide ourselves away with make-believe. I learned that the hard way.
I think life can be ugly and painful and short. And we should fill it with as much fun, and laughter, and love as we can find.
Chat ends.
Mine only became a little more problematic because of the whole... Void thing.
You make a fair point. I think when it becomes a replacement for the real thing, it's a problem. I'm not suggesting that.
You're right. And I hope it's something we remember, as we go forward together in... whatever this is that we're in.

You know, I found Eleanor, Velimir, Aoi, and Amir, playing hide-and-seek with Flare and Lizzie. (Quincy said he wasn't allowed to play because the bastard was cheating and was using his scope to see through walls.)
They were all looking at me worried I was going to be upset I caught them mucking about when they should be doing something useful.
I was more upset that I wasn't invited. Heh. But I had to put on the grumpy leader face and pretend I was upset that the posts were left unmanned, etcetera.
But Amir has his games. Aoi has On-lyne. Even Kaya has her stickers and her Jinymon, for all that the world has forced adulthood on her too soon.
Is there a point you're trying to make?
I think it's something you could get back, if you tried. Finding joy in toys and games, I mean.
Honestly? I'm not even sure. Only that I feel like I'm missing something that's been gone from my life for a very long time.
I can just hear the laughter now. But I suppose that's really what's holding me back, isn't it? Embarrassment.
I'm not sure if I can ever get it back. Or if it's too far gone. But who knows. With enough time, maybe anything is possible.
I'm not sure it's possible to get it back, even if I could push through the momentary shame. But who knows. With enough loops, maybe anything is possible.
Chat ends.
Chat ends.
